response.passage: In India, the right to vote is a fundamental pillar of our democracy, granted to every citizen who is at least 18 years old, regardless of their education, wealth, or social status. Voting is a voluntary exercise of your democratic right, meaning no citizen is legally punished or fined for choosing not to cast a ballot. During an election, you visit a polling station where the process is designed to be completely private. The Electronic Voting Machine (EVM) is a standalone device that is not connected to any internet or Wi-Fi network, ensuring it cannot be hacked remotely. When you press a button for your chosen candidate, a VVPAT machine prints a paper slip that you can view through a glass window for seven seconds to verify your choice before it drops into a sealed box. This slip remains with the election officials as a record and cannot be taken home by the voter. Furthermore, the Election Commission functions as an independent constitutional body that operates separately from the ruling government or the Prime Minister. The Model Code of Conduct serves as a set of guidelines for fair play during elections, and while it is not a criminal law that sends people to jail, it ensures that those in power do not misuse government resources to influence the outcome of the election.
response.summary: India's democratic system ensures that every adult citizen has the right to vote through a secure, private, and independent process. The Election Commission maintains fairness, while technology like EVMs and VVPATs protects the integrity of the ballot.
